# Scan 96 — reader A, SP92

## Content and scope
The page continues a sentence about the objects V indexed by pairs. It treats incomparable indices with X written **metrisable**, equal indices, and distinct comparable indices; then it gives an intersection definition labeled **(98)** and restricts the indices to a flag ordered strictly increasingly. The last paragraph calls the protopos “pierres de construction” and speaks of forming others through a limit expression with the written qualification “finies si I fini”. Its final indexing formula uses Drap(I). A starred, diagonal marginal addition refers to homotopic protopos V with superscript Z “plus bas”. These are descriptions of the page’s claims, not verified results.

## Source lettering and boundaries
The page has no authorial title, date or page number at its head. The thin grey **95** at the lower left belongs to another hand and is preserved as a margin item, not as an authorial mspage. The candidate’s scan marker is editorial. H’s introductory note, repeated-number comment and description of the marginal note are editorial and excluded. No numbering sequence was repaired: the written display label remains (98).

The right paper edge clips the opening word’s final b/l group and the final return of d’introduir. Their full shared witness spellings are not completed beyond the visible ink. The recorded blind audit retains these clipped readings without completing off-page letters. The acute accent supplied by C in métrisable is absent from the enlarged source; metrisable is retained. The literal short form str. keeps its visible stop. The quotation is enclosed by two high ticks on each side, not French guillemets.

## Revisions and attachment
There are five cancelled groups in the main text: the uncertain old verb between on and aura; the resolved et immediately after the first phi; a cancelled V term after enfin with an unresolved ij/j index; an old d/donc/On group before the separately uncertain live comme/aura; and the resolved cancelled V_i before i<j. The first group is not a live trouve followed by a second deletion as H parses it. Both live aura occurrences in the earlier cases remain independent of their strikes. The blind audit replaced the earlier short-word hypotheses after enfin and before i<j with the V terms. The old verb and old d/donc/On interiors remain uncertain. No strike extends into the following live formula or replacement.

The star after the main-text protopos calls the diagonal left-margin note. The note is live throughout and its opening and closing parentheses are preserved. Its text is not inserted into a different sentence. The marginal final p’s descending stroke approaches the main-text opening before pour éviter; the status of an independent opening parenthesis remains uncertain and has its own blind box. The closer after the lower phi is visibly a right curly brace although the opener before sinon is a parenthesis; this mismatch is retained.

## Mathematical rereading triggered by the witnesses or small signs
Both empty signs were reread with their surrounding formulas: each is a small loop traversed by a long axial descending stroke, transcribed as phi. The diagonal sign is not silently converted to the witnesses’ standard empty-set glyphs. Their meaning here is the empty case described by the sentence.

The entire (98) display was reread. Its first index has a closed 0; the left continuation is one horizontal rule, while the continuation between the two intersection signs comprises two separated short rules. The displayed increasing chain likewise has two short continuation rules, and its numerical subscripts are 0 and 1. The set of indices, the final definition of d, and the marginal V subscript were each read as complete expressions. The first two have one continuation rule between written commas. The marginal index has only the comma after i_0, then one rule and i_n, with no second comma. These literal marks are represented by mathord minus strokes rather than normalized three-dot ellipses; the notation does not claim subtraction.

The limit sign was reread in its full phrase and in a tip detail because C gives an underline and H a direct-limit arrow. The short terminal backward/downward leg supports a right arrow at medium confidence; the candidate uses varinjlim. No categorical claim was inferred to decide the ink. The recorded blind audit retains this whole expression and its medium-confidence directed-limit reading. The complete final V_d / d=(...) membership formula and the marginal V^Z formula were inspected, including their indices, commas, parentheses and exponent.

No proof check, computation or mathematical use was performed by reader A; check_events is empty. Root’s separate checks, if any, are not attributed here.

### Root check of the reduction to flags

The pairwise definition on scan095 gives V_{ij}=V_i intersection V_j. Commutativity and idempotence of intersection justify V_{ij}=V_{ji} and V_{ii}=V_i. Under the metrizability setting used there, an incomparable pair has empty pro-neighborhood intersection; hence any finite tuple containing such a pair has empty total intersection. A tuple of mutually comparable indices can be sorted, and repeated indices removed, without changing the intersection. These observations justify the page's reduction to strictly increasing flags. They do not decide the written limit mark or the letters of the verb. The recorded visual audit retains the directed-limit reading at medium confidence and resolves the verb as bornera. See CHECK_EVENTS statement150-096-flag-reduction.

### Blind reading corrections

The crossed group after enfin is a V with an unresolved ij/j index; the later crossed group before i<j is V_i. Both replace the earlier short-word readings. The verb after mais on se is bornera, with separately visible ra. The clipped right-edge words are not completed. The literal closing brace after phi remains a brace, although the opening delimiter is a parenthesis. The slanted marginal phrase remains et des protopos homotopes, with exponent Z and plus bas.
